incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: RED_THRESHOLD fired for us-east-az10 (nic-degeneration)

pagerduty: incident 983274 opened - auto-page sent to @alex oncall

alex: acked. I'm looking. seeing spike in nic errors from the host telemetry.

maya: acked and joining. what's the customer impact?

alex: CPU fine, but NIC packet drops and soft resets on a subset of nodes. metrics: `packet_drop_rate` jumped to 12% for az10, p50 latency up 350ms -> p95 > 3s for short seq workloads.

jon: noted traffic pattern — concentrated on model shard s-14 (short context chat). routing layer retries are amplifying failures.

alex: running quick diagnostics:
```
# on control plane
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l zone=az10 -o wide
ssh node-12 'dmesg | tail -n 50'
ip -s link show eth0
```

maya: logs show `e1000e` driver resets on node-12 and node-15. NIC firmware reported: "EEE link flaps".

sre-lead: escalating to hardware team (eng-runtime). @eng-runtime can you confirm if this is a known firmware regression? Also start failover plan for affected shards.

eng-runtime: acknowledging. spinning up routing fallback for shard s-14 to us-east-az11 canary. will throttle new sessions into az10.

alex: enabling routing policy: `route.policy: prefer(az11)->fallback(az10)` and activating `degraded-mode=true` for shard s-14 to reduce KV cache reliance.

product-ops: heads-up to support: customer-facing incidents page should be prepared (likely partial regional degradation, not global outage).

pagerduty: 983274 escalated to SRE Lead after 5m no progress.

jon: applying canary rule:
```
POST /admin/routing/update
{ "shard": "s-14", "policy": "shift-30p-az11" }
```

incident-bot: routing-update job started (job-id 9f3d).

maya: can we confirm client session safety? we need to avoid fronting clients to az11 if KV cache mismatch causes hallucinations.

alex: switching to read-only KV fetch for newly routed requests; using prefix cache validation. should avoid divergence.

eng-runtime: node-12 and node-15 taken OOS for NIC firmware outage. reboot loop observed; we are contacting infra for rack-level HW replacement.

pagerduty: 983274 acknowledged by @alex and @maya; auto-escalation suppressed.

product-ops: drafting incident banner: "Partial service degradation in US East (az10). Some chat sessions may experience higher latency or transient errors. We are routing traffic away from affected hosts."

alex: quick impact numbers: approx 9% of total prod requests in the region were hitting s-14; of those ~35% saw elevated latency or transient 5xx. overall customer impact estimated ~3.2% of total platform requests during spike window.

sre-lead: good. this is regional partial outage not full region failover. proceed with controlled remediation.

maya: monitoring telemetry: after routing shift p95 latency in az10 for s-14 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s; overall error rate for s-14 down from 13% -> 2.1%.

eng-runtime: replacement NICs scheduled, ETA 28m. keeping nodes OOS until firmware validated.

alex: enabling additional autoscale for az11 to soak extra load: `scale.policy.s-14 = +20% immediate`

incident-bot: note added to incident 983274: "routing fallback activated; hardware replacement in progress; degraded mode enabled for s-14"

jon: alerting customers with active SLAs: list owners in #customer-success and ping high-traffic tenants.

product-ops: posted banner and opened status page (link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/983274).

pagerduty: incident 983274 - current status: Mitigated (partial). oncall handover scheduled in 2h to @jon for monitoring and postmortem prep.

maya: notes for postmortem:
- root cause: NIC firmware regression causing link flaps under certain jumbo-frame loads
- mitigation: route fallback to az11, degraded read-only mode for KV, OOS affected nodes
- customer impact: ~3.2% total requests, targeted to shard s-14 primarily
- follow-ups: firmware rollback/patch validation, improve auto-failover for shard hotspots, run traffic shaping tests on NIC firmware matrix

alex: assigning owners: `postmortem_owner=jon`, `fw_owner=eng-runtime`, `support_comm=product-ops`

sre-lead: handoff to @jon now. Alex/Maya - please drop any runbook gaps in the incident doc.

jon: taking over monitoring. will collect logs and schedule postmortem with all owners.

eng-runtime: will stay on call until nodes validated, will publish firmware test results to the incident doc.

incident-bot: incident 983274 status updated -> monitoring; next update expected in 20m or on new significant event. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks everyone. staying reachable if things change.

maya: good job. closing Slack loop, will follow on postmortem.
